canonical_question: How does the formation of σ-phase at 900 °C specifically alter the mechanical properties compared to the 700 °C behavior?

question_variants.question: How does the formation of σ-phase at 900 °C specifically alter the mechanical properties compared to the 700 °C behavior?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text confirms the formation of sigma-phase at 900 °C at cell structure boundaries but does not provide data or discussion comparing its specific effect on mechanical properties versus the 700 °C behavior.

answers.answer: The document notes that sigma-phase was formed at the cell structure boundary for samples deformed at 900 °C, but does not explicitly link this to specific changes in mechanical properties compared to 700 °C.
answers.measurement_outcome: Sigma-phase formed at cell structure boundary
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparative mechanical property data provided for 900 °C vs 700 °C
evidence_spans: SLM-built HEA had a face-centered cubic (FCC) single-phase random solid solution.
In addition, SLM-built HEA was composed of epitaxial growth grains, dislocation network and nano-sized oxides.

Room- and high-temperature compression tests confirmed that SLM-built HEA has outstanding mechanical properties in all temperature ranges compared to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs reported up to the present.
